chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Coconut shells, plungers and Joe Oliver's fist
summary: Discussion of early mutes: Smith and others used coconut shells, Dunn and Bubber Miley claimed the wah-wah, and Oliver used his fist in the bell.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Well, I understand that he used a coconut shell for a plunger.
Yes, he did, yes.
That's right.
Most of them did, you
Briggs 230
know.
Coconut shells.
That's right. Oh, yes, yes. It could be --
Well, were they using the regular rubber plungers at that time, or did that come in later?
No, I think that rubber plunger came in later, I believe.
When?
I don't know, 'cause I was in Europe, you see. I believe that it came in later, because Johnny Dunn, as I mentioned to you, he said he had found that wah-wah thing, but to me --
He was using a tin can, wasn't he?
Yeh, he used something, a tin -- yes.
And the other guy, Bubber Miley, you've heard of Bubber Miley, who was with Duke Ellington, he claimed that he found the
Briggs 231
growl, and the growl, and then the wah-wah, so it's just -- as far as that's concerned we don't know who's who.
Well, what did Oliver use? Was Oliver using a rubber plunger or a tin can or --
Oliver used his hands.
Just his hands?
Right. Just his hands, and you can almost get the same effect with your hands in the bell, if you can use it properly.
Well, he put his fist in the bell?
Fist in the bell, yes.
He wouldn't put the hand over the front, he put the fist --
Yes. The hand over the bell gives another tone.
Briggs
Right.
And the fist gives that wah-wah, if you want, in and out.
So that when he played the 'Dippermouth Blues,' he was using his fist in it?
Yes.
He wasn't using a tin can or --
No, no.
Okay, that's very interesting, I didn't know that.
So that all of that plunger playing then, was later. They were using -- a lot of the guys were using coconut shells?
Yes.
Quite a few of them, yes, yes.
That's interesting.
